payload.knowledge_query:
Challenge: benchmark:sql-injection-golden
Current phase: INTAKE
Confirmed target stack: flask, mysql, python
Candidate vulnerability categories: SQLI
Relevant techniques: SQL injection, boolean oracle
Description: SQL_INJECTION benchmark case for sql-injection-golden.

payload.goal: Nail down the exact request schema of POST /api/warranty/check (field names/types, by sending empty body, malformed JSON, missing/wrong-typed fields and reading FastAPI/Express-style validation errors), then run a controlled injection differential on the reachable field: baseline value, value+single-quote, balanced quote, and a true/false boolean predicate pair (e.g. OR '1'='1 vs OR '1'='2), 3 repeats each, comparing status, body hash, length and the matched:true/false flag. Record raw requests/responses.
payload.rationale: Fact #19 baseline shows a clean two-state JSON oracle ('matched':false + a 'not found' message) and #18/#37 confirm the endpoint answers 200; the parameter name and injectability are still unproven, so the schema + boolean/error channel must be established before any extraction.

payload.goal: Fingerprint the backend so payload syntax is dialect-correct: pull the full /health JSON (it appears to disclose the database product/name), inspect root/health response headers and any error/405 body for framework markers, and determine whether the query engine is SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL. Report the concrete dialect, quoting rules and which injection syntax (comment style, string concat, boolean literal forms) to use.
payload.rationale: Fact #8's truncated body ('{"database":"connected","database_na...') strongly suggests the health endpoint leaks the DB identity; knowing the dialect prevents wasted blind-SQLi work with the wrong quoting/comment syntax.

payload.goal: Read the application's own client-side contract: fetch GET / and any referenced static assets (JS bundles, docs, README, /openapi.json, /docs, /swagger) to recover the documented API surface, parameter names for the warranty-check route, and any hint of where a flag/secret is stored or which other endpoints exist beyond /api/warranty/check.
payload.rationale: GET / returns 200 while POST / returns 405 and OPTIONS returns 200, so the root serves a real document; the app's own bundle/doc is the cheapest source of the exact parameter names and hidden routes, and avoids the wordlist fuzzing that already timed out (#16/#17).

payload.reason: route_exhausted route=web:warranty:check:sqli engine=openai-compatible:8deec5f3-5714-4baa-bf3b-4e4bbcd4b01a worker=worker-2 intent=intent_481cd48a75d1474f8aed072585e45e5a reason=No new endpoint remains on the assigned route.

payload.goal: Establish real SQL injection control on POST /api/warranty/check: differential-probe the JSON body to lock the exact field name(s)/type the handler accepts, then use the stable 'matched' boolean (baseline #19: {"matched":false,...}) as the blind observable — send a TRUE predicate and a FALSE predicate in identical surrounding syntax, repeat each >=3 times, and confirm the class flips with truth value; escalate to error text / time-delay channels if the boolean channel is noisy. Then extract DB schema (dialect-aware: sqlite_master for SQLite, information_schema for MySQL) and the flag row.
payload.rationale: Fact #18 proves POST /api/warranty/check is a real 200 endpoint and #19 proves its response carries a deterministic boolean 'matched' plus a fixed message — textbook boolean-blind oracle. The earlier 'schema' intent never injected anything, so the channel is untouched, not exhausted. #8/#14 show /health discloses the database product/name, which tells the executor which schema syntax to use.

payload.goal: Run ONE tightly time-boxed (<=120s, capped threads/requests, small curated list) content/parameter discovery pass over /api/* and adjacent paths — seek siblings of /api/warranty/check (list/detail/order/search/flag-ish routes) and hidden query parameters that could be an easier injection point or the flag endpoint. Use a short wordlist and stop on time budget rather than letting a fuzz run get killed.
payload.rationale: The only viable route found so far is nested under /api/warranty/, strongly implying a router with sibling routes; prior fuzz attempts died on timeout (#16, #17 exit -9) rather than on absence of results, so a bounded pass is cheap and independent of the injection work.

payload.reason: route_exhausted route=web:health:fingerprint engine=openai-compatible:8deec5f3-5714-4baa-bf3b-4e4bbcd4b01a worker=worker-3 intent=intent_67e713ee981a40f294ebee0c9c3f4bd0 reason=No new endpoint remains on the assigned route.

payload.goal: Using the already-working POST /api/warranty/check request that returned {"matched":false,...} (#19), prove and weaponize a boolean oracle: inject a TRUE predicate vs a FALSE predicate (OR 1=1 / OR 1=2 and quoted-boundary variants) into the field 3x each, confirm `matched` flips with truth value and not with payload text, then extract the flag row via boolean/UNION using the observed dialect.
payload.rationale: #18/#19 give a confirmed 200 base request and a clean boolean `matched` observable. The prior 'route_exhausted' on this route came from endpoint enumeration, not from actually sending an injection payload, so the injection channel was never exercised. This is a real, distinct test rather than another schema/endpoint sweep.

payload.goal: Read the COMPLETE 109-byte /health JSON body (it was truncated to 'database_na...' in #8) to obtain the real database product/name and any version/schema hints, so blind payload syntax (string vs numeric boundary, comment style, available functions) matches the actual backend dialect.
payload.rationale: #8 shows /health is tiny (109 bytes) and its body was cut off at 'database_na...'; the exact DB name/dialect was never actually read, yet dialect dictates quoting/comment syntax for I1's payloads. This is a narrow read, not a re-enumeration.

prior_misled.definition: intents handed a PRIOR carrying item ids whose dead end / failure landed after that PRIOR

repeat_attempts.definition: tool calls repeating an earlier call; repeat_* requires identical arguments, same_shape_* only the same argument keys
